name: Wrist Classic — Leather
tagline: Azan on the wrist, five times a day.
desc: An azan watch sized for a santri's wrist: a 36 mm case that fits under a sleeve and a soft leather strap that disappears on the arm after a day.

It vibrates quietly for each of the five prayers and sounds the azan when you hold the lower button, so it stays silent through a lesson and still calls when it matters. Set the city once and it keeps Fajr through Isha on its own, seven days on a charge.

name: Wrist Steel — Bracelet
desc: Brushed stainless steel with a folded clasp, for the teacher who is in front of a class all day and cannot keep looking at a phone.
Vibration is the default, so the azan arrives without a sound. The dial carries the Hijri date under the hands, and the bracelet adjusts without tools.

name: Wrist Sport — Silicone
tagline: For kerja, jalan and the gym.
desc: A 42 mm silicone-strap watch built for heat and water: rain, wudu and washing up are all fine down to 50 metres.
The dial is readable at arm's length, which is the point when your hands are full or you are counting laps.

name: Wrist Slim — Dress
tagline: Six millimetres thick under a cuff.
desc: Six millimetres thin, so it slides under a shirt cuff instead of catching on it — the watch for a wedding, a hafalan ceremony, or a day of meetings.
Under the quiet face it carries the same azan engine as the rest of the range: five calls a day, silent or audible, plus the Hijri date.

name: Wall Classic — Rattan
desc: The clock most people picture when they hear azan clock: a 12-inch rattan case, brass hands and a face you can read from the other side of the room.
Full azan for all five prayers at masjid volume, or a light chime for a bedroom. Two AA batteries last about eight months and keep the time through a power cut.

name: Wall LED — Digital
tagline: Three-inch digits you read across the room.
desc: Three-inch LED digits with the prayer name and the Hijri date on the same screen, so you read the next prayer without walking closer.
It comes with a remote, so volume and city are set from the sofa. Eight city presets cover Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya and Makkah among others.

name: Wall Square — Masjid
tagline: Built for a musalla wall, loud and simple.
desc: A square 15-inch face made for a musalla wall, with volume high enough to fill a room of forty people.
The iqamah timer counts the minutes between the call and the standing prayer, so the jamaah knows when to line up without anyone watching a phone.

name: Wall Grand — Mosque
desc: The largest face in the range at 16 inches, with a remote and a memory that keeps every setting for eight months without a battery.
It shows the temperature beside the time, which the caretaker uses to decide whether the fans go on before the jamaah arrives.

name: Table Wood — Desk
tagline: Stands on a desk, tilts to any angle.
desc: A desk clock on a wooden base that tilts to whatever angle you are reading at — beside a laptop, on a shelf, or on the shelf in front of a class.
Same azan engine as the wall clocks: five calls a day, silent mode for study hours, and a face that stays readable in a lit room.

name: Table LED — Bedside
tagline: Dims itself at night, lights up at Fajr.
desc: A bedside clock that dims itself after lights out and brightens at Fajr, so you wake to a lit face instead of a dark room and a sound.
The alarm asks you to sit up before it goes quiet — the difference between waking for Fajr and switching it off half asleep.

name: Table Mini — Travel
tagline: Folds flat, fits a bag, keeps the times.
desc: Eighty-four grams that fold flat into a bag: for mudik, for a trip to another city, for the room you are staying in and do not want to be late in.
It charges over USB-C, remembers eight cities, and holds its settings while it sits switched off in a pocket.

name: Table Grand — Brass
tagline: Brass base, the one you keep for years.
desc: A weighted brass base that stays where it is put, with a rounded face everyone in the room can see from a chair.
It is the one on the shelf that outlives the rest: brass that ages instead of wearing out, and the full azan engine with the Hijri date.
